questions.problem:
Expressed as a polynomial in terms of $x,$ the length of Dan's plot of land is{{field-1}}
yards.
questions.worked_solution:
The width of the plot is $x+2$  yards, and its area is $2{x}^{2}+4x$ square  yards. Since the $\text{area}=\text{length}\times \text{width},$ we factor the expression for the area to find the length.

First, we find the $\text{GCF}$ of the two terms:

$$
\text{GCF}(2{x}^{2},4x)=2x
$$

Then, we rewrite each term in the original expression as a product with the $\text{GCF}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}+4x & = \\ (2x\cdot x)+(2x\cdot 2)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we write the $\text{GCF}$ outside the parentheses and keep the remaining terms inside:

$$
\begin{aligned}(2x\cdot x)+(2x\cdot 2) & = \\ 2x(x+2)\end{aligned}
$$

 

As a result, we conclude that the length of the plot must be $2x$ yards.

questions.worked_solution:
To find the length of Brenda's plot of land, we need to factor the expression ${x}^{2}-4.$

First, we write the expression as a difference of squares:

$$
{x}^{2}-4={x}^{2}-{2}^{2}
$$

Then, we factor the expression using the difference of squares formula:

$$
{x}^{2}-{2}^{2}=(x+2)(x-2)
$$

As a result, we conclude that the length of the plot must be $x-2$ yards.

Dan's neighbor to the south, John, has a land plot of area ${x}^{2}+x-12$ square yards, as shown in the picture. Given that the length of John's plot of land is $x+4$ yards, what is the width of the plot in terms of $x?$

John's plot width is
{{field-1}}
yards.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the required width, we need to factor the expression ${x}^{2}+x-12.$

First, we find the factor pairs of the constant term $(-12).$ The constant term is negative, so that means one of the factors is negative, and the other is positive:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & \times (-12) \\ (-1) & \times 12 \\ 2 & \times (-6) \\ (-2) & \times 6 \\ 3 & \times (-4) \\ (-3) & \times 4\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we find which factor pair adds up to the coefficient of the linear term $1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}1+(-12) & =-11 & \times  \\ -1+12 & =11 & \times  \\ 2+(-6) & =-4 & \times  \\ -2+6 & =4 & \times  \\ 3+(-4) & =-1 & \times  \\ -3+4 & =1 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

Using the factor pair identified above, write the linear term as $x=4x-3x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+x-12 & ={x}^{2}+4x-3x-12\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we factor the first two terms and the last two terms separately, and then factor the expression completely:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+4x-3x-12 & = \\ ({x}^{2}+4x)+(-3x-12) & = \\ x(x+4)-3(x+4) & = \\ (x-3)(x+4)\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we conclude that the width must be $x-3$ yards.

questions.problem:
If $x=10\,\text{yd},$ what is the area of John's land plot?

Area $\,=$
{{field-1}}
${\text{yd}}^{2}$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the area, we have to evaluate the polynomial ${x}^{2}+x-12$ at $x=10.$

So, we substitute $x=10$ into the polynomial and simplify: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+x-12 & = \\ (10)^{2}+(10)-12 & = \\ 100+10-12 & = \\ 98\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area is $98\,{\text{yd}}^{2}.$

When $x=10\,\text{yd},$ the dimensions of John's plot of land are $14\,\text{yd}$ and $7\text{yd}.$ A water pipe goes diagonally from one corner to the opposite, as shown above. Find the **exact** length of the pipe.

The length of the pipe is 
{{field-1}}
yards.
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that we have a right triangle with legs $a=14\,\text{yd}$ and $b=7\,\text{yd}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14153614/assets/4b28a9cd713d5098bb735236f3b9d96eaefaffb09a165a951bbbee56b25a1451.png)

Let $c$ be the length of the hypotenuse. Then, according to the Pythagorean theorem, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}^{2} & ={a}^{2}+{b}^{2} \\ c & =\sqrt{{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the values for $a$ and $b$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\sqrt{{14}^{2}+{7}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{196+49} \\  & =\sqrt{245}\,\text{yd}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Dan purchased his land for $160$ thousand dollars. The value of the land increases by $10%$ each year. How much will Dan's plot be worth after $5$ years? Round your answer to the nearest thousand dollars.

After $5$ years, the land will be worth approximately 
{{field-1}}
 thousand dollars.
questions.worked_solution:
The land initially costs $160$ thousand, which increases at a rate of $10%$ per year.

$10%$ as a decimal is $0.1.$ Therefore, an increase of $10%$ corresponds to multiplication by a factor of

$$
1+0.1=1.1.
$$

Therefore, we have:

* After $1$ year, the value will be $160\cdot (1.1)$ thousand dollars

* After $2$ years, the value will be $160\cdot (1.1)^{2}$ thousand dollars

* After $3$ years, the value will be $160\cdot (1.1)^{3}$ thousand dollars

* After $4$ years, the value will be $160\cdot (1.1)^{4}$ thousand dollars

* After $5$ years, the value will be $160\cdot (1.1)^{5}$ thousand dollars

Evaluating the expression for the value after $5$ years, we get the following:

$$
160\cdot (1.1)^{5}=257.68≈258
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.

Therefore, after $5$ years, the land will be worth approximately $258$ thousand dollars.

questions.problem:
The value $V(t)$ of Dan's plot of land, in thousands of dollars, can be modeled by the function $V(t)=160\cdot (1.1)^{t},$ where $t$ is the time in years since he bought the land. What is the growth in the value of the plot over the first three years? Round your answer to the nearest thousand dollars.

Dan's land grew in value by approximately
{{field-1}}
 thousand dollars over the first three years.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the growth in the value over the first three years, we need to find the value after $3$ years and then subtract the initial cost:

$$
V(3)-V(0)
$$

In the previous part, we were given the initial value of the land:

$$
\begin{aligned}V(0) & =160\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find $V(3),$ the value of the land after $3$ years:

$$
\begin{aligned}V(3) & =160\cdot (1.1)^{(3)} \\  & =160\cdot (1.331) \\  & =212.96\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the growth in the first three years is

$$
\begin{aligned}V(3)-V(0) & =212.96-160 \\  & =52.96 \\  & ≈53.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the growth in the value of the land over the first three years was approximately $53$ thousand dollars.
